Level 21, also known as "Numbered Doors", is the current 22nd level found in the Backrooms.

Description
Level21og2

Endless hallways stretch beyond infinity.
Level21og2

Level 21, also known as "Numbered Doors" by wanderers, is an expansive, currently without a determinable sized labyrinthine complex made up of a vast array of hallways, corridors, rooms, and many others alike. The most notable consistency that can be observed across Level 21's appearance is how most, if not all corridors possess equally-spaced doors on each side, generally maintaining their outer appearance to be identical throughout the entirety of Level 21; these doors have been said to appear as standard, framed metal doors which have all been measured to height around 7ft tall, and widen approximately 40 inches, as well as always possessing a shiny metal doorknob on its right side. The level's structural appearance mostly covered with carpet, usually colored in 'modern' colors ranging from white to gray to tan and many others. The walls are generally constructed from a balanced mix of plaster and concrete, giving them an oddly smooth texture and appearance.

The primary lighting on this level is provided by ceiling lights that appear to repeat themselves on the plaster ceiling or either regular office ceiling tiles. The tiles can occasionally be arranged either vertically or horizontally. The lights are fluorescent; however, unlike fluorescent lighting in Level 0, they don't provide sound and can take on various shapes and forms. The light switch on the wall is also linked to the ceiling and can be turned on and off; however, some do not have one. Lights rarely fade or flicker at random times, and certain lights may be constantly off without shining again. There are also windows in the level, with another side shining white light or a void with stars, can also appear to light up the hallway, but they cannot be damaged or opened and are most likely to be seen in The Lobby Room.

Vents and air-conditioning systems on the ceilings filter the level's air and provide a fresh breeze throughout rooms and corridors; people say Level 21 is very comfortable; the temperature on the level can reach 18°C. There are also multiple fire sprinklers and fire alarms, so even though it is unlikely that the level will catch fire, they will activate if you set it on fire. Additional decorative items such as fire exits, fire extinguishers, plant pots, chair rails, and wall lights can also be found.

The architecture of Level 21 is complicated due to the various passages and turns that frequently result in dead ends and intersections. The halls are consistently constructed in an orderly manner according to the model. The halls' design and color scheme are constant, giving the observer the feeling that they are familiar at times. Every hallway on Level 21 has a unique layout and design, which could involve things like the width of the hallway, the color of the walls and the carpet, as well as the size and shape of the fluorescent lights. Every corridor has a different vibe; some resemble hallways in hotels, offices, schools, etc.

The Lobby Room
The Center of Level 21

A large lobby surrounded by an endless hallway.
The Center of Level 21

The Lobby Room is a sizable room where several passageways lead. These interconnecting rooms allow people to move to new passageways with different styles and layouts than the ones they just left. The architecture room is perplexing due to its appearance, which seems like multiple rooms or hallways sharing space, making a peculiar structure comparable to a labyrinth. The fact that The Lobby Room has a particular appearance that is shared by the halls that link to it.

Structures in The Lobby Room are utterly pointless and unnaturally bizarre, including the misplaced doors along with the closed room with no entrance, the walls and pillars that are positioned in the middle of the room to function as an overload threat, the excessive amount of light sources and the variety of fixtures that place in the same space, the different color and pattern of carpets that lie in the same location, and others that can be explicitly stated. Using these unnatural constructions, The Lobby Room was formed by sharing an area of each hallway space to link each other and allow people to walk to another place.

The Lobby Room is the location where you can find a variety of furniture and items, such as chairs and desks, along with bookshelves and other reading materials near the wall. You may also get supplies and unrelated objects here. They consist of food, weapons, almond water, and level keys. Additional objects have only been sighted on rare occasions. It is also known that exits may be discovered here due to the size, and the exit door also has a number sign indication, making it easier to find.
Beyond The Doors
Level21-Room

Comfort room to rest inside.
Level21-Room

Doors are sporadically positioned on either side of the hallway, ranging from closely spaced to far apart. A hidden room seems to be there beyond the door. Because of the unpredictability, each room is quite varied and almost unique. Although most of these rooms are made to imitate hotel rooms, offices, classrooms, and empty spaces, others may be created differently. Being non-Euclidean in nature, they can look large and allow for the fitting of ridiculous size within without impacting the remainder of the hallway, which is typically a non-Euclidean area.

The door may occasionally be locked even though it could have been opened previously. However, this would never happen if there were someone inside. The doors will finally be opened if enough time has passed; this might take from five minutes to two hours or even more. This occurrence seems to change something about the inside of the room, as though it were doing so. Wanderers report that artifacts and objects appeared within the chamber afterwards, and that the occasion appeared to clean the room and repair any damage that had happened. The room's appearance may change, and whatever was in the room will vanish. So it is not suggested to keep valuable objects inside the room and use the room on the level as a residency permit.

Certain rooms have an oblique effect that enables them to mimic the design or aspect of a corridor, such as a carpet and ceiling light. Wall lights, fire extinguishers, exit signs, and other items indicated previously in the hallway and lobby room may be found inside the room. On the other hand, furniture and ornamental objects that are generally put in rooms might emerge in the hallway near the room containing these furnishings, however, this is most likely to occur in The Lobby Room.

Shifting Area
Level21og

The hallway starts to shift into darkness.
Level21og

Certain areas of the level could gradually transform into a dilapidated, abandoned passageway. The rotting and split wall revealed the inner flesh of the shattered concrete wall, the stained and torn carpets revealed the dirty tiles, and dust from the broken concrete could be seen and smelled everywhere. It is not advised to stir up the dust since it will fill the air and make breathing difficult for everyone nearby. Most of the fluorescent lighting in this area emits less light, making the space darker and less luminous. Some of the lights are either damaged or out of operation. The majority of the doors in this location are locked and inaccessible, but a few may be unlocked and lead to regular rooms that are similar to regular ones but distinct from the filthy conditions along the corridor.

In certain places, power outages might result in total darkness throughout the area. A shattered wall can expose clusters of pipe and cable. The wires carry high voltage, and the pipes contain an unknown liquid that appears hazardous and should be avoided; however, the pipes and wires are hidden behind the wall at a safe distance, and no one has died at this level yet.

This area differs from other areas of the level in that other areas will experience phenomena that result in any damage or dirt within the level being repaired or cleaned, but not in this shifting area, where nothing changes when something happens. This information led to the conclusion that the shifting area used to be standard and clean like other ones, but with time it suffered damage and included wanderers. There were scratch marks and other signs on the wall that didn't appear to be caused by people, leading to the belief that there were once entities on this level.

“
“In the midst of awakening, my mind by now knows nothing more than a vast hallway, repeating itself indefinitely. The walls extend forever in all directions. The light shines in the distance, covering up the darkness. The side doors, as well as the carpet pattern, keep repeating like my own thoughts.

The atmosphere is nothing more than the mere emptiness of an interminable hallway. In this isolated and unsettling place, I can feel a sense of familiarity with the simplicity of the space.”

Endless Dream
I was by myself in the dimly lit corridor, surrounded by an endless length of nondescript walls that seemed to go on forever. My footsteps reverberated as I walked, each step a reminder of the vast emptiness that surrounded me. My mind was filled with both wonder and uncertainty; time and space seemed to warp and twist in unsettling ways.

21-6

Dark halls with isolation atmosphere.
21-6

I continued walking, my attention concentrated on a faraway spot that beckoned me forward. At each stride I took, the walls surrounding me shifted and transformed, taking on new patterns and forms. Some of them were ornate and intricate, covered with deftly designed patterns and motifs that moved in the flickering light of the torches that lined the ceilings. Others lacked any distinctive features or marks and were plain and featureless.

I felt surprisingly at ease despite my strange surroundings. There was a sense of calm in the cold air, a feeling of silent meditation that seemed to seep into my bones. It was as if I had been transported to another plane of existence, one where the worries and concerns of the outer world were nothing more than distant memories.

I moved along at a steady, leisurely pace. I had no clue how long or how far I had been traveling. This location exuded a sense of timelessness as if the past, present, and future were all interconnected. It was a liberating sensation to be released from the limitations of the real world.

The doors, the carpet pattern, and the ceiling seemed to repeat at every intersection, leaving me exhausted and wondering what this place might be. A bedroom with a soft bed and other ornamental items awaited me beyond the door, providing me with the familiar impression that I used to reside here. A lovely bed made me want to rest in this liminal space, but I kept walking indefinitely.

21-5

Dim light in liminal space.
21-5

The place begins to dim with some light, but the isolation and loneliness remain. It feels like I'm walking into the depths of this place. I begin to lose sight of my shadow, but I can see a few lights in the center of the darkness as it attempts to brighten the hall but instead creates a liminal light level. A window next to me is visible despite the pitch black. On the other side, I can't see anything; it seems to be a void full of stars, which makes the corridor view nostalgic.

Beyond numerous doors, all appear to be hotel rooms and share a similar look. The light shining through the door lit up the hallway as I kept opening the door. At the end of the hallway, there is one that is distinct from the others; I can see the number of doors and wonder where it could take me. The atmosphere gets brighter as I move toward the door while contemplating until I approach it...

— Charles Schmidt
August 20th, 2019

Colonies and Outposts
There are no known colonies or outposts in this level.

“
“Outposts once existed here, but unfortunately they were short-lived.”

Failure Plan
M.E.G. used to plan to construct outposts at this level since it is the connection between all levels in the Backrooms. The strategy begins by sending explorers to the entrance — Warp Tears on the wall — in Level 20 to access Level 21. Once inside, they try to find the door with the numbers on it and mark the location of the exit. As soon as they discovered the exit to Level 4, they started constructing outposts to transport supplies and valuable resources from one level to another. Yet when a M.E.G. member sent supplies and other items, one of the explorers reported that the exit was unexpectedly changed to Level 37, which led to the failure of the outpost plan.

M.E.G. is currently using this level to investigate random and undiscovered levels. This level is also used as a rest stop when traveling, although M.E.G. never plans to have any groups or outposts settle permanently here. Although there are no colonies or outposts, there may be groups of wanderers or explorers that can be found, though it is difficult to find them due to the small group sizes and the infinite level.

— Tiffany Lauren

Entrances and Exits
Entrances
Various tears in the walls of Level 20 can be entered to reach this level. These Warp Tears can be encountered occasionally on Level 11, Level 9, Level 6, and Level 13. Climbing a withered tree in one of Level 121's islands can take you here or noclipping at any level can also rarely lead you here.

Exits
The level is considered a hub to access other levels, as a few of the doors are marked with a random 3-digit number; entering that door will take you to a random level, such as Level 22, or many other levels; however, this does not work for negative or anomalous levels due to unknown circumstances. The exits will change levels and the number of doors will change as time passes—between two hours and two days. As a result, if you find any escape and travel to any safe level, you must act quickly before the exit vanishes. Noclip on the floor also takes to Level -1.

“
“In some of the level's rooms, there was a low-pitched sound that seemed as though nothing had happened, yet it was the sound of some equipment functioning. To hear the sound a little more, you must place your ear to the wall—it worked in some rooms. I'm curious about what's behind the wall and what this is.

Every level in the Backrooms, including this one, has a phenomenon called "protection" that keeps the area appearing clean at all times and cannot damage anything there. So I almost gave up on my investigation into this, but then I realized that some areas in the level are absent of a phenomenon called "Shifting Area," which causes the area to become run-down and abandoned and can cause damage inside the area.”

Addendum
Here is some information I got from my investigation and research.

Numerous pipes interconnect with a strange machine behind the wall and beyond the ceiling. The pipes in the level are all linked to these unusual machines; the pipes are all brand new, undamaged, and made primarily of traditional materials such as lead, PVC plastic, copper, or any other. Yet occasionally they are built using unconventional materials like wood, steel, pressed ash, glass, granite, and an uncountable number of other materials. These pipes transport a variety of liquids, primarily ethylene glycol (antifreeze), and have similar components to Level 2's pipelines.

21-2

The hallway changes and fluctuates over time.
21-2

These liquids in the pipelines provide a massive amount of energy to an anomalous machine; as it receives more, it works harder. These hardworking machines make a loud noise when they operate, but we can't hear it because, despite its appearance, the drywall is highly effective at soundproofing. The pipes and machines in the shifting area are nearly always damaged and broken, with no functioning, but occasionally some are normal, filling the region with loud machine noise.

These machines appear to have displays and have constructed the rooms' contents. If there is dirt or any damage inside the room and no one is inside, the machine will work by locking the doors and cleaning or fixing anything in the room. It also provides some additional items and objects that are helpful to wanderers. There is no phenomenon inside the room that will protect and clean any content; instead, these machines will do it. But if no one is in the room for an extended period, the machine will completely alter the look of everything there. It is not advised to use this level as a permanent address since anything of value would eventually vanish. The unworking machine will influence the room, making it look vacant with a small interior; this occurrence is common in shifting areas. Further study of these abnormal technologies is on hold because of a lack of progress in understanding their other actions, which are often unpredictable.

21dark

But in the end it all leads to The Void.
21dark

The machines construct exits by making the exit area similar to or the exact same as the level to lead to. The room will build a path into the level itself by gradually grading it. It is uncertain what the number has to do with the exit since when the exit gate changes, the number will change also. According to a notion, each level has its own number, such as doors that marked 105 go to Level 0. Nonetheless, each wanderer claims that the numbers on the exit doors that lead to the same level are contradictory, rendering this unconfirmed.

Additionally, it is theorized that this level is the mirror of Level -1 and that the level also has an exit to Level -1; it is also theorized that Level -1 exists below the Level 21 floor. Level 21 is also said to be connected to The Void because it could lead to any random positive level in The Backrooms—it cannot lead to a negative or anomalous level—and some wanderers claim to have encountered The Void while breaking through the ceiling in a shifting area. implying that the void is beyond the ceiling of Level 21.
— Researchers Andrew

Revision as of 4/19/2011: Level 22: "Parking Hub"
1
1
Sd-hexagon
Survival Difficulty: Class 1
»⠀Safe
»⠀Unstable
»⠀Minimal Entity Count
Level 22 is assumed to be linked to Level 11 due to sharing a similar city-like atmosphere.

Description
22

An image of Level 22.
22

Level 22, also known as “Parking Hub”, resembles a parking lot garage with multiple floors that stretch for approximately 500 square kilometres. The level is well lit up by fluorescent lights that occasionally buzz, albeit quietly and flicker. Curiously, the level is surrounded by a black abyss of some sorts, which many believe leads to Level 6. However, this hasn't been confirmed as no wanderer has entered through the abyss yet. The most prominent feature of Level 22 are the cars; they are capable of turning on but cannot drive. In addition, they typically contain Almond Water and other essential items in the back seats or the trunk.

Similar to the parking garages from The Frontrooms, Level 22 consists of multiple floors with each having the same physical appearance; each floor does not have any difference aside from its layout and different colonies living on each floor. A peculiar feature of Level 22 is that the further you go away from the center of the level, less cars will appear. This continues until you eventually reach the border of the level, where wanderers will encounter the aforementioned abyss. Many wanderers this far from the center of the level have claimed to experience hallucinations of other entities and cars speedily driving towards them, only to disappear near "impact". The reasoning for the hallucinations is unknown, though the M.E.G. is investigating the phenomenon. It is advised to be cautious around this part of the level, especially since this section is not as well documented as the rest of the level.

Throughout the level, several elevators can be found. Each elevator will take you to various floors, ranging from Floor 1 to Floor 20. In most instances, these elevators have the option to take you to different levels, a popular pick being Level -6 and Level 87 due to both being habitable levels. However, most wanderers don't like the idea of being stuck in an inescapable paradise, so majority of wanderers who find these elevators reside in Level -6.

Entities
Facelings are quite common within the level as they tend to wander around the level.

Colonies and Outposts
Many colonies and outposts have been established due to Level 22 acting as a rest stop.

The Athestin Empire
Has a population of 20-30;
Inhabits the 17th floor;
Willing to trade and let wanderers into their group.
The Looters
A group that breaks into the cars found in Level 22 and takes all of the items for personal use or for trading;
Unguarded;
Open to trading resources;
Friendly and may accept new members;
Inhabits the 14th floor;
15-30 members.
Outpost 22
An outpost that specialize in helping hurt or dying wanderers;
Open to trading and accepting new members;
They claim that they found a giant hole that leads them to Floor 5 to Floor 7;
Inhabits near the giant hole that leads to Floor 5, 6 and 7;
Population of 25-35 members.
Entrances and Exits
Entrances
The most common way to enter Level 22 is by going into a parking garage in Level 11.
Going through a parking garage entrance in Level 32 leads here.
Elevators in the lobby of Level 21 may teleport you here.
Bunkers of Level 41 can lead here.
Exits
By using an elevator that leads to levels instead of floors, wanderers can make the selection to enter Level -6, Level 1, Level 4, Level 21, Level 23, and Level 87.
Destroying a car has a chance to take you to Level 23.
Revision as of 10/29/2015: Level 22: "Ruins Left Behind"
“
“I was with my colony, when suddenly the level collapsed. I saw my friends fall into the endless Void while others got crushed and slowly die. I was the only survivor…”

— One of the few wanderers that survived when Level 22 collapsed.

E
E
Sd-hexagon
Survival Difficulty: Class 4e - Environmental
»⠀Unsafe
»⠀Unstable
»⠀Several Non-Entity Hazards
General Description
Lvl22

An image of Level 22.
Lvl22

Level 22, also referred as "Ruins Left Behind", resembles an abandoned parking garage with yellow support beams and several damaged cars scattered across the level. Multiple wires, deactivated fluorescent lights and signs are found hanging on the ceiling. In addition, there are potholes, debris, ash and dust on the floors, which may pose as tripping hazards if the wanderer isn't cautious enough of their surroundings. Like parking garages from The Frontrooms, Level 22 consists of multiple floors. However, each floor appears to worsen and darken the lower you go; this also applies to the further you go from the center of the level.

One of the anomalous properties of this level comes from its cars. They are typically found 350 meters away from the entry point with some being accessible. These cars seem to take on the appearance of a car from the wanderer's favorite car manufacturer. For example, if a wanderer likes Toyota, then the cars will appear as any car sold under the Toyota brand, whether new or old. If the wanderer doesn't have any favorite car manufacturer, then the cars will take on the appearance of any random car from any random car manufacturer. Within the cars are damaged tools, such as hammers, and Liquid Pain bottles. Despite these damaged cars seeming ordinary, the anomalous properties become apparent when you enter a car with a shattered or non-functional headlights; by doing so, an entity will appear in the backseat or right beside you whether the car. It is advised to immediately exit the car and run far away as you can.

Entities
Anethikas, Smilers and Car Lurkers are the only documented entities reported in Level 22.

Colonies and Outposts
Due to the unstable and deadly environments of Level 22, creating a colony or outpost is infeasible.

Entrances and Exits
Entrances
Finding a parking garage in Level 11 and then entering it will take you here.
Going through a parking garage entrance in Level 32 will lead you here.
Elevators in the lobby of Level 21 may teleport you here.
Bunkers of Level 41 can lead here.
Sometimes, a parking garage entrance in Level -6 can be found, entering it will lead you here.
Exits
Descending through multiple stairways will lead you to Level 59.
Using a functioning elevator that takes you to levels instead of floors will take you to Level -6, Level 1, Level 4, Level 21, Level 23, and Level 87. It is not recommended that you take this exit as the elevators may not function properly and instead may take you to Level 404 and The Corrupted Instability.
Revision as of 6/12/2018: Level 22: "Polluted Ruins"
“
“Another unfortunate case in the hands of the Level -6 infection. We shall contain the virus in its home level, or else it will spread and devastate all of the Backrooms.”

— A wanderer who managed to survive entry to Level 22 after being polluted

22 Custom Class5
Survival Difficulty: Class 5e - Environmental
>> Unsafe
>> Unstable
>> Entity Infestation
>> Numerous Environmental Hazards
General Description
22RuinsLeftBehind

Level 22 in the aftermath of the Level -6 infection.
22RuinsLeftBehind

Level 22, also known as "Polluted Ruins", is another unfortunate case of the Level -6 infection. The level resembles a flooded abandoned parking lot with rusted support beams and ceilings, polluted water, collapsed floors, and visible formation of stalactites on the ceiling. Aside from the noticeable state of disrepair the level is in, one of the most noticeable features of the level is the liquid that the level is flooded with. This liquid has been dubbed as "Nuclear Infection", which leads many to believe that the liquid came from Level -6 via an entrance. This liquid should be avoided in any circumstances, as staying in it will dissolve wanderer's flesh, causing immense pain and potential death; This explains why human remnants are rarely found in Level 22. In addition to the many hazards of this liquid, it can also produce a green smog. This green smog should not be inhaled in as it can block your lungs, causing you to suffocate to death; if the green smog doesn't suffocate you fast enough, it will begin to dissolve your insides.

Several damaged and corroded cars can be found, which along with the level are in terrible condition. As a result from the Nuclear Infection and the entities inhabiting Level 22, the interior of these cars are completely empty, with only the metal body of the car itself being the only remnant. As listed previously, elevators are present here. Wanderers can make the selection to pick what floor they want to travel to, but is highly recommended that you do not use these elevators as they do not work properly as they did before; using an elevator will cause it to free fall and land in The Corrupted Instability.

Entities
Level 22 consists of Nuclear Membris, Skin-Dissolvers, Corrosive Moths, Death Fishes, and Car Lurkers. All of the entities prior to the infection of Level 22 were either killed off by the entities now inhabiting the level, dissolved by the liquid, or managed to escape the level.

Colonies and Outposts
Due to the deadly and harsh environments, creating a colony or an outpost is infeasible.

Entrances and Exits
Entrances
Finding a parking garage in Level 11 and then going in it will take you here.
Going through a parking garage entrance in Level 32 will lead you here.
Elevators in Level 21 may teleport you here.
Bunkers of Level 41 can bring you here.
A parking garage entrance in Level -6 can be found, entering it will lead you here.
Exits
Tunnels in Level 22 may seamlessly lead to Level 49.
Descending down through stairways will lead you to Level 59.
Using an elevator will cause the elevator to free fall and bring you to The Corrupted Instability.

ntities
Car Lurkers
Description
Car Lurkers are entities that mainly inhabit the higher floors of Level 22. This entity only appears right after wanderers enter a car with a shattered or non-functional light.

Behavior
As previously mentioned, Car Lurkers only appear once a wanderer enters a car with a non-functional or shattered light. The entity will appear either at the back seat, the trunk, or in the front seat right beside you depending on whether the car has a back seat or not. Car Lurkers have the ability to distort reality and the laws of physics if it comes into contact with a wanderer. Likewise, it can distort pretty much any other lifeforms, such as other entities. As soon as a lifeform comes into contact with a Car Lurker, the matter making up the lifeform will annihilate into pieces, and they'll reach the brink of death. Therefore, it is best to avoid this entity in any circumstances. If wanderers were to encounter one, they should get out of the car and run as fast as they can away from the car. Fortunately, the entity's abilities nor the entity itself cannot reach you outside of the car.

Biology
Due to their vaporizing and law distorting abilities, not much of the biology of the entity has been studied, aside from physical appearance. They appear as black humanoids with no arms, assumably amputated legs, and sunken white eyes. Due to their assumably amputated legs, Car Lurkers aren't able to walk, solely relying on teleportation for transportation, albeit they cannot exit the car they're in for unknown reasons. In addition, Car Lurkers cannot speak, nor communicate with wanderers, but do let out a scream whenever it first appears or when the wanderer first notices it.

Do and Don’ts
Do
Avoid cars with non-functional or shattered headlights.
Get out of the car as soon as you see a Car Lurker.
Avoid interaction with it at all costs.
Don’t
Let a Car Lurker touch you.
Try to fight it; it can easily vaporize you.
Discovery
Car Lurkers were discovered 2 days after the 10/13/2015 incident on 10/15/2015 after a member of The Looters went to retrieve any remaining supplies from the cars. The wanderer in particular stumbled across a car with shattered headlights and decided to search the car for any supplies. Once the wanderer got in, a Car Lurker appeared right beside him, as the car in question didn't have a back seat. The wanderer was subsequently terrified and jumped out of the car immediately.

Oddly enough, Car Lurkers were completely unaffected by the 4/6/2018 incident, the reason likely being that since they have the ability to vaporize lifeforms, any entities that attempted to harm them were most likely vaporized.

M.E.G. Notice: The information below has been protected as it contains classified details that should not be released to the public.

M.E.G Database Login Form

Gary

Access Granted!


v File 1 - Incident 10/13/2015: 22V
Incident 10/13/2015: 22V
IntegerroomsParking

A supposed image of Floor B taken by a M.E.G. unit.
IntegerroomsParking

On 10/13/2015, M.E.G. discovered a floor beneath Floor 1, this floor was named "Floor B". Floor B was similar to the other floors, but with a much darker environment. The floor contained huge amounts of high explosives and containers filled with gas. When M.E.G. Units were travelling through Floor B, they encountered a wanderer that appeared to be frightened and afraid, the said wanderer was also holding a gun and shot at the units but missed, unfortunately, the bullet hit the gas containers causing a fire, soon the fire reached the high explosives which detonated. Due to high explosives being found practically everywhere on the floor, the explosions detonated the other explosives, this quickly spread causing too much damage for the level to handle and multiple floors began to collapse; due to this event, several people fell into The Void while others were crushed and fell to their death leaving with only a handful of survivors, despite the remaining people that survived from falling into The Void and being crushed, only 2 of them have managed to escape and tell the tale. After Level 22 was destroyed, M.E.G. found out that Level 22 was in floating in The Void with nothing to support it from preventing the level to fall. After this event occurred, Floor B and Floor 13 to Floor 20 have fallen into The Void including the wanderers that we're inhabiting those floors. While M.E.G. units were travelling through Floor B, they have experienced intense hallucinations such as entities and heavily armed men running towards them and suddenly fading away on near impact, this also may be the reason why the wanderer who was found on Floor B shot at the units, of course, this may not be true at all as he also may have mistook the units as hostiles.

v File 2 - Incident 4/6/2018: 22-6
Incident 4/6/2018: 22-6
On 4/6/2018, M.E.G. was blocking off all entrances from levels that led to Level 22 one by one. They eventually found a corridor which led to a locked door, which was an entrance from Level -6 that led to this level. However, M.E.G. didn't know about this at the time. The explorers decided to attempt to unlock it via breaking it open. After a few attempts, the explorers were successful in opening the door. However, an influx of liquid began to subsequently enter the Level 22 in a rapid pace. The explorers immediately tried to block off the entrance again, but to no avail, as it was too late, and were swept away by the liquid. Along with the liquid, the virus within Level -6 managed to find its way into Level 22, starting the process of polluting the level.

After 1 hour
The liquid began to dissolve weaker structures and objects of the level, such as tires, Almond Water bottles, and signs. In addition, support beams and the ceilings began to rust & corrode, likely a property of the liquid or the virus. Fortunately, every wanderer managed to evacuate the level in time.

After 1 - 2 days
The majority of the liquid from Level -6 had been drained into Level 22, submerging Floors 1, 2, 3, and 4 completely and partially flooding Floors 5, 6, 7 and 8. This sped up the process of the pollution of the level and the rusting and corrosion of the support beams and ceilings. All of the entities from Level -6 managed to enter Level 22, causing more damage and pollution to the level in the process. On top of that, most, if not all of the entities in Level 22 prior to the infection would have most likely either been dissolved by the liquid, killed off by the new entities, or have somehow escaped the level.

After 2 months: 6/6/2018
Most objects, aside from the cars have been dissolved or corroded by the liquid. Some cars and support beams were destroyed by the new entities inhabiting the level. Moreover, certain parts of the floor and some support beams have collapsed due to deterioration. Stalactites began to grow on certain parts of the ceiling.

Since then, the level has stayed mostly the same, apart from more stalactite growth and damage done by the entities inhabiting the level.

> Description:
Level23new

A photograph of the interior of Level 23.
Level23new

Level 23 appears to be an infinite factory, although it appears to be in a state of disrepair and abandonment each of the walls appear to be rusted, occasionally having holes in them. When entering these holes, one will be sent to a small hallway, which resembles a claustrophobic cave, after traveling through these caves, one will end up in another room of Level 23. A few of the fluorescent ceiling lights appear beaten, with visible weapons such as chainsaws, knives, hammers, and maces lodged deep into them. In addition, various firearms, such as revolvers, Semi-automatic pistol, assault rifles, shotguns, and sniper rifles can be found on the floor, or on a part of the machines. It is also possible to find massive puddles of water on Level 23's floor.

Each room of Level 23 is cluttered with various forms of machines, each of which will produce things such as firearms, objects, entities, rooms, and entire levels. While each machine appears destroyed, they function perfectly fine, despite their appearance suggesting otherwise. These machines are powered by one's most prized memories. As such, tampering with a machine will result in it activating, resulting in you losing your most prized memory. After that, you will become deeply confused on what happened. However, you will eventually realize that you have lost your most prized memory. As such, you will become depressed, before committing suicide. As such, Level 23's suicide rate is extremely high. In theory, it could be possible to cure this effect with Almond Water. However, Level 23 is completely devoid of Almond Water. In addition, when one enters Level 23, their whole supply of Almond Water will disappear or expire. As such, this remains unconfirmed.

Level23OG

Overgrowth of Level 23.
Level23OG

Various forms of floral life can be found in Level 23. From previous documentations of Level 23, the floral life has overgrown the factory after accidentally being put into one of the machines. Most of the floral life consists of moss, vines, and Venus flytraps. The moss, when stood on for too long, will turn wanderers into a garden statue, before they eventually become part of the moss. Vines in Level 23 have been described as "Weed-whackers if they whacked humans instead of weeds". When one gets close to a vine, the vine will lash out at them, before throwing them against a wall, killing them. Venus flytraps will appear to be much larger, about the size of a Smiler. When a Venus flytrap detects a wanderer, it will emit crying sounds, which will lure wanderers to them. Once a wanderer is close enough to the Venus flytrap, it will eat them alive, killing them. There is also a mist of sorts that converts wanderers that enters the mist into more Venus flytraps. However, this mist can easily be repelled with a gas mask.

>> Storage Rooms:
Some doors in Level 23 will appear to be a shade brighter than usual doors. In addition, there will also be the sound of knocking on the other sides of these doors. Entering these doors will lead to small storage rooms. Upon first glance, the rooms appear to be regular storage rooms. However, the lights of these rooms will eventually shut down completely. Once this occurs, various TV screens will appear, playing the most prized memories of various wanderers. This is when a wanderer realizes in horror that Level 23's machines work off of prized memories.

>> Higher Floors
On occasions, it is possible to encounter robotic claws. When getting near one, they will grab wanderers, and throw them at the ceiling with blunt force. Due to the extreme amount of force, one will break the ceiling and enter the Higher Floors of Level 23.

The Higher floors of Level 23 share a more modernized and fixed look. As such, all of the ceiling lights have been repaired, puddles are now extremely small to the point of being barely noticeable. These features include the high amounts of other forms of technology, along with jumbles of wires. Going in these wires will result in one being trapped in them, before being electrocuted to death. However, there are still some properties from the Lower floors of Level 23, such as the floral life and machines.

Level 23's upper floors are described as a "somewhat habitable location", and is said to be "a place to relax from the horrors of Level 23". Moss takes far much longer to convert one to a garden statue, vines and Venus flytraps are absent, and the mist is absent. However, it is possible to encounter entities in this section. The chances of encountering an entity is really rare, however.

> Entities:
Entities in Level 23 include hostile adult Facelings, Smilers in dark areas, Skin-Stealers, and Insanities.

> Colonies and Outposts:
>> Backroom Colonists - Site Factory:
Located on the higher floors of Level 23, approximately 100 miles north.
A large room, which houses around 14 members.
Stocks up on supplies, such as food, first-aid kits, and gas masks.
Guarded.
>> M.E.G Outpost:
Located 10 miles south from the spawn area of Level 23.
Contains various beds, along with food and healing supplies.
Friendly.
Highly guarded.
Willing to trade.
>> The Outcasts:
A hostile community consisting of 14 members. The Outcasts roam both floors of Level 23 to search for guns, and will occasionally combine them to create new guns. If a member of the Outcasts notices one, it will call all the other Outcasts. If this occurs, this means that they are on the hunt, and you're most likely going to die. From recent studies, a few members were former members of the Backroom Colonists, and have been exiled for their crimes.

> Entrances and Exits:
>> Entrances:
An elevator in Level 22 will send one to Level 23.
No-clipping through a ceiling tile that "feels off" in Level 0. This ceiling tile will appear to be a shade darker than Level 0's regular ceiling tiles.
Entering a factory called "FACTORY NO. #023" in Level 11 and the Outpost section of Level 998.
Breaking the floor in Level 28.
Climbing to the top of a metal pole sends one to Level 38.1.
Entering a large factory-like space on Level 268 sends one here.
>> Exits:
No-clipping through the ceiling will send one to Level 24.
Going out doors that are engulfed in bright lights will send one to Level 11.
Finding A door that is titled "Mall" would send you to Level 59.
Staying for a very long time in a building will cause the level to fade into Level 575.

entries.content:
Level 24: "Extraterrestre"

Dreamscape 2

Where am I...?
LEVEL
24

> Description
Space-art (level 24 rewrite)

An image of Level 24.
Space-art (level 24 rewrite)

Space level 24 rewrite

Another said image of the level.
Space level 24 rewrite

Level 24 is an infinitely desolate, liminal, dark, alien-like landscape. Rapid shifts and changes ensue chaos to the level. Furthermore, the level seemingly follows Euclidean geometry but completely ignores known science, making Level 24 unpredictable and dangerous.

The level is seemingly a collection of all alien and extraterrestrial landscapes enticed together, stretching on seemingly forever or at least too big to map out. Despite whatever variations occur in the atmosphere, landscape, gravity, and weather, the level seemingly retains its dark, gloomy appearance. This phenomenon is exceedingly intriguing, and currently unexplainable.

The landscape becoming gaseous, temperature turning down to absolute zero, and gravity suddenly increasing or decreasing have been common hazards in the level. To elaborate further, another difference many wanderers reported is the variations in the sky. One may see clear constellations with towering planets that should not be scientifically possible at such close distance (May induce severe symptoms of Megalophobia to all wanderers); this phenomenon would usually mean said landscape lacks an atmosphere, but since Level 24 completely ignores science, whether or not one can breathe in said environment depends on chance; other times atmosphere would thicken so much to the point of impeding vision, but one may suffocate on seemingly space void.

Dreamscape 2

Am I out of the liminal hell? Is this space...?
Occasionally, crystals of different colors can be found on and beneath the surface, each having unique properties depending on their coloration. These crystals are a source of intrigue for many wanderers, but also pose a significant danger due to their unpredictable nature. Similarities between the crystals found in Level 117 and the crystals in said environment have been pointed out by many researchers, but no research have been done to provide conclusive evidence.

Red
Blue
Green
Yellow
Orange
Purple
DescriptionThe red crystal has a thermogenic effect, heating up surroundings efficiently and sometimes providing warmth. The amount of heat the crystal produces varies from one another. However, the crystal may cause burns if one is too close.
> OPEN GALLERY

Dreamscape 2

I walked on and on through the hopeless, dead, landscape...
Objects would fall from the sky at random intervals regardless of orbital range. Meteors and Comets are common hazards in Level 24. It is advised to take cover when such a phenomenon happens. Planets and other celestial objects in the sky can collide with each other on random intervals. This creates a similar effect, as debris will rain down into Level 24.

Planetary Collision
Planetary Collision

A artist's depiction of a Planetary Collision (may not be accurate).
Planetary Collision

Astonishingly, planets seen on the horizon can also collide with the landscape. The collateral damage varies since Level 24 completely disregards science (Creating huge impacts sending trillions of tons of rocks into orbit, touching the surface harmlessly like a beach ball on the water, or anything else are all possible scenarios). Although it is hard to envision such humongous objects crashing down, the landscape is so vast (possibly infinite) that such a phenomenon can happen. Information about the planetary collision is scarce because most wanderers who viewed it within a certain distance (even if far away enough to be unharmed) will go either blind or insane trying to comprehend such as massive structure. This phenomenon can cause intense fear to all wanderers regardless of symptoms of Megalophobia.

Void 001
VO-001, also known as the lost planet, is a planet surrounded by a nebula and the only object seemingly drifting in the void. Due to its identical properties to Level 24, it is presumed that VO-001 is a small portion of Level 24 that no-clipped into the heart of the void by unknown means. Further investigation has been conducted by several major groups, including The Backroom Colonists, The Kauer, and The Anti-Entity Group. Surprisingly, the most prominent faction, The M.E.G. has remained silent the matter.

> Entities
Though abnormal footprints have been found in the dust and rocks on 'Level 24', suggesting there may be something "lurking about", no entities have been recorded present on 'Level 24'. Despite this, dreams of Entity 12 is almost certain if wanderers sleep on said level, which is highly unrecommended.

Dreamscape 2

Wait I see something in the distance!
> Colonies and Outposts
BlewPlanet

A black hole in the horizon.
BlewPlanet

Due to the environmental dangers and its difficulty to exit, setting up a base is incredibly foolish and near impossible. Despite this, The M.E.G. has attempted a total of three mining expeditions to obtain the crystals in Level 24; however, the results were underwhelming and the project was abandoned.

The M.E.G., The Backroom Colonists, The Kauer, and The Anti-Entity Group have also sent exploration teams to the level, in the hopes of documenting Level 24 to a greater extent, and temporary bases has been set up for this reason. The only team that returned, the Kauer's Omega squadron, discovered a structure anomaly seemingly inconsistent with the rest of the level, now designated as Situation 25.

Dreamscape 2

A glitching structure... it seems like I'm still stuck in the Backrooms...
Situation 25
Level25

The only image of this base.
Level25

Situation 25 is an anomaly in Level 24, discovered by The Kauer research organization. Situation 25 appears to be a futuristic structure reminiscent of the halls of Level 15. The exterior is seemingly transclucent while also glitching and shifting in appearance. Though Situation 25 may vary moderately in appearance, the structure retains its bright, clean, futuristic theme. While a small portion Situation 25 does appear above ground, most of the structure lies underground, sprawling expansively for unknown lengths.

The interior surroundings seem to solidify as one enters; however, the interior is still highly unstable, and is prone to many shifts, glitches and other hazards. While still similar to level 15 in design, the interior structure seems slightly altered and modified to suit the nuturing of alien plant life. The artificial gardens within Situation 25 are a marvel to modern engineering. Despite being in a dimly lit environment, the LED lights that replace the sun provide enough energy to maintain the flourishing flowers and trees. Some sections with the overgrowth of canopy has created miniature forests of grassy paths, alien fauna, mutated redwoods, and even streams of clean drinking water.

As one goes further in, despite still retaining the clean futuristic design, the condition of the area seems to deteriorate. Lights are dimer and flicker more frequently, the floor and walls may glitch more often, futuristic machinery starts to go haywire. The plant life becomes more decayed, as if mistreated or abandoned for a long time. The database suggests that wanderers not to approach the area, as the Kauer has only mapped out a small portion of the uppermost sections. Further expeditions into the deeper sections of Situation 25 have all failed to return.

Dreamscape 2

I'm getting tired... there's no food or water. I can feel my consciousness slipping away...
> Addendum
> Close B.C. file
<COMMENCE>

*Several higher ups are seen discussing below the treetops of Level -599*

(Overseer of security) Darren Nakamura: There has not been this much casualties since the great war. All exploration squads sent to Level 24 were compromised. Not to point fingers, but Laurel, you're responsible for this.

(Overseer of exploration) Laurel Yew: This is hardly my fault, I TOLD you going into Level 24 was a bad idea. We don't have the cohesion and professionalism of the M.E.G. or the Kauer!

(Minister) Chase X: All the lives lost, only for the Kauer to discover the only significant documentation. These were people who had friends and families! They were people of our big family, The Backroom Colonists!

(Overseer of security) Darren Nakamura: (snorts) Cut the fake talk, we need to discuss what actions to take next!

(Minister) Chase X: (Offended) I'm being genuine!

(Overseer of exploration) Laurel Yew: You two, stop it! Plus, I don't think their sacrifice was in vain, we did receive signals that may imply information!

(Overseer of regulation) Darren Nakamura: Yes... an SOS signal.

*Laughter*

(Overseer of exploration) Laurel Yew: (flustered) NO! You all don't get it! Don't you see? SOS signals are usually sent when under attack by a hostile presence! When was the last time someone sent a SOS signal for environmental dangers? According to data, SOS signals sent for hostile presence is up to 70 percent, while only 20 percent sent for environment dangers, 9 percent sent for miscellaneous reasons and 1 percent sent by accident.

(Overseer of regulation) Lee Hollingsworth: What does this imply?

(Overseer of exploration) Laurel Yew: That it is HIGHLY probable entities exist in Level 24! Especially when abnormal footprints have been found in the surface. Not to mention, we also received a voice message via grade 2 quantum messaging.

(Overseer of development) Mitchel Texter: We did?

(Minister) Chase X: (frowns) Why didn't you tell us?

Lieutenant Morro: Sorry minister, it took a while for the message to be transferred, due to Level 24's distant and unstable nature. I received the message right before the meeting and reported this to Overseer Yew.

(Overseer of security) Darren Nakamura: Work faster next time!

(Overseer of exploration) Laurel Yew: (Rolls her eyes) You can't "work faster" to receive a message!

Lieutenant Alan: At any rate, the message does bear pivotal information, the exploration leader reported spotting something abnormal in the distance. This message came from the same device that sent the SOS signal.

Lieutenant Morro: Not to mention, this message was sent before the SOS signal, but due to its file size, we had a delay receiving said message.

(Overseer of development) Mitchel Texter: What does this mean?

(Overseer of exploration) Laurel Yew: If I were to guess, the group was attacked by some entity! Usually, one would not have a chance to even send a signal if environmental dangers got the better of them.

(Minister) Chase X: Hard to say... I feel like we're missing some pieces of the puzzle here, Laurel, anything else to report?

(Overseer of exploration) Laurel Yew: Uh, not as of now, no.

(Minister) Chase X: Then I suggest we put this matter aside for now, we don't have enough evidence to offer something conclusive.

<END LOG>
> Close Kauer file
<COMMENCE>

*A blank room lights up, with a single operative sitting on a chair*

Artificial intelligence: Please state the purpose of your visit.

Unnamed operative: I am here for the mission debrief of Situation 25.

Artificial intelligence: Continue.

Unnamed operative: Situation 25 at first bears a significant resemblance to Level 15, almost identical if not for some slight alterations.

Artificial intelligence: That being?

Unnamed operative: Mainly plants and more greenhouse technology, it is not exactly level 15, but too similar to be a sub level.

Artificial intelligence: Continue.

Unnamed operative: As my team went down deeper, the surroundings became darker, the condition of the base worsened. Plant life were decayed, as if left abandoned for a long time. There has even been broken down machinery lying around, some of the automatic gates were destroyed... saying the place was uncanny is an understatement.

*Silence, AI processing said information*

Artificial intelligence: Could Jovials be a possible cause of this condition?

Unnamed operative: Perhaps, in fact, the surrounding were very similar to what a jovial infested area would be like, but it feels like the whole environment changed, not just the structure being destroyed, the deeper one went, the more paranoid one feels, as if we're being watched, yet heat signals didn't pick up anything near by.

<END LOG>
> Close A.E.G. file
<COMMENCE>

*Two shadowy figures meet up in a dark corridor*

AEG 1: The place where no sun shines.

AEG 2: Level 6.

*The two figures shake hands*

AEG 2: This loss means more to us than the other factions.

AEG 1: Indeed, we need to be more cautious next time. Some of our best men perished there. However, our path is clear.

AEG 2: Our path is clear, all entities shall perish.

AEG 1: We received nothing from the only exploration team we sent. However, one of the four groups is evidently hiding something.

AEG 2: It couldn't be the Colonists could it?

AEG 1: The group picking daisies and doing sing alongs in their treehouses? They would disband before hiding information from the database . . . no, I'm talking about the M.E.G.

AEG 2: How can you be so certain?

AEG 1: Don't you think they remained awfully quiet after the Kauer discovered Situation 25? Not to mention ignoring the lost planet. They're hiding something we don't know...

AEG 2: Still, that is not enough reasoning to suspect them.

AEG 1: According to inside sources, a M.E.G. squadron that survived was brought in for interrogation, yet everyone believes that the Kauer's Omega squadron was the only team that survived. Is that enough?

AEG 2: What is it they're hiding that we don't know?

AEG 1: I'm not sure, but especially with abnormal footprints found in the level, I suspect there is some enigmatic monster in need for elimination.

<END LOG>
> Close M.E.G. file
<COMMENCE>

*An Impresario walks inside a retro futuristic office room*

Impresario S: I’ve always wondered, we’re exactly are we?

The First: (Chuckles) Does it matter?

Impresario S: Well, curiosity always gets ahead of me, which level are we in? Level 154 wouldn’t make sense would it?

The First: No, I suppose not... we’re not in a level, this is ah, my own domain.

Impresario S: I’m not sure if I understand, but it doesn’t matter, I’m here to talk about this.

*The Impresario places down several files on the desk*

Impresario S: I don’t get it, something is discovered in void, IN THE VOID! VO-001 obviously has ties with Level 24. Then there’s situation 25! Something is brewing! Three of the four major factions have been undertaking research, and we, the most prominent by far, just pretend we don’t know anything about it?

The First: (amused) The Colonist have the most manpower, I’m sure they’ll take care of it.

Impresario S: Sir, with all due respect, I’m not here to joke around, if anybody has the capacity to understand this, you know it's either us or the Kauer, the Colonists have always been abundant on resources, but lacks in organization and knowledge. What’s up with the act? You’ve avoided this subject during the council gatherings and we’re actively suppressing this information amongst our ranks for no reason at all!

*Silence*

The First: Sylas-

Impresario S: Please, I’m one of your most trusted friends!

*The first slumps down on his chair, face twitches, slightly annoyed*

The First: It is futile to do any research related.

Impresario S: Why?

The First: Situation 25.

Impresario S: What about it?

The First: VO-001 is indeed a minuscule portion of level 25, it was cast into the void due to the migration of Situation 25… please, why do you think the base is so similar to level 15?

*Silence*

The First: (sighs) Because it is a part level 15.

Impresario S: You mean it was a portion of level 15 just like VO-001 is to Level 24...?

The First: No… to be exact, Situation 25 is still part of Level 15. A series of events somehow managed to no clip a small part of level 15 into Level 24, if that makes sense…

*The Impresario abruptly leans forward, hands on the desk*

Impresario S: (surprised) That is possible? No-clippage of a level?!

The First: Apparently yes, because of this, a portion of Level 24 was replaced and consequently faded into nothingness, the void. This is the reason why the environmental dangers have not destroyed the base yet, because it's not really there. This portion of level 15 is in a rather complicated situation… you can imagine it being trapped in a limbo, or a purgatory, not much different from us being trapped in the backrooms.

Impresario S: I-

The First: To put it simply, Situation 25 is still level 15, but just a part that only manifests its self in Level 24, which consequently pushed a portion of Level 25 into the void, now designated as VO-001.

Impresario S: Do the other Impresarios know of this?

The First: Some do, I have no qualms in informing all of them. However, I need some time to digest all this information myself… you see, the Kauer wasn’t the first to discover Situation 25.

Impresario S: It was us, wasn’t it?

The First: (laughs) Surprisingly no, a team from the Colonists was the first, but they went in too far. Brave, but woefully unprepared… our squadron were the next to discover Situation 25.

Impresario S: What made us more prepared?

The First: The corporal was more cautious and contacted higher ups immediately, his squad stayed on the surface until further instructions. Eventually, a larger group made its way down into depths.

*Silence*

The First: Something was down there.

Impresario S: Elaborate.

The First: Hard to say, the members who came back were traumatized, none of them could recall the events in detail. Of course, all this information had to be suppressed.

Impresario S: Why?!

The First: The survivors seemed horrified about recounting the events. Some directly told the interrogators to "stay silent" on the matter. Researchers suggests that it is too much for a human brain to handle, and that discussing the event frequently might initiate some sort of cognitive hazard. Spreading the information may ah . . . cause further complications.

Impresario S: What about the Kauer?

The First: After said events, the Kauer discovered Situation 25 officially and safely documented it to the database. They didn't look deep enough, although further attempts to explore the area has all failed, I think they took the cue and canceled the project. The AEG and the Colonists are too far behind to complicate the situation. We are at a standstill right now, and it is in our best interest to keep it that way, it is the best that we leave that place alone.

Impresario S: I- I see...

The First: Now, let us have some tea shall we?

<END LOG>
> Theories and Hypothesis
Theories on what the level truly is, origination, and other interpretations of this liminal environment.

The Titan Hypothesis
This theory suggests that the level is not infinite, but a huge anomalous planet estimated to be as big as a Dyson sphere. The surrounding planets, which are naturally smaller, all orbit and crash into the landscape. However, judging by the infinite maze like corridors of the backrooms, and its anomalous nature. It is highly improbable that Level 24 is a planet instead of an anomalous liminal space.

The Infinity Thesis
The Infinity Thesis is the mainline explanation. This Theory suggests that the landscape is infinite, just like most spaces in the backrooms, and it, just like the rest, represents a unique liminal theme. This is further proven by the fact that the level always retains its dark desolate environment despite whatever changes occur. Since the landscape is infinite, meaning it is not a planet, some deem it as flat. However, this is not true, since no one can comprehend what shape infinity is.

The Outlander Approximation
This theory suggests that this level is one of the oldest levels in what we understand as the backrooms due to its primitive environment not resembling anything man-made. Although carvings on cave walls and relics have been found that are believed to be evidence of an ancient civilization.

The Many Worlds Construct
This theory suggests that Level 24 is not one infinite landscape, but a collection of planets that wanderers no-clip to. This explains the extreme variations in environment, since wanderers are traversing differing planets. Smaller planets would constantly crash down to bigger ones while rotating each other in chaos, similarly to the three body problem, but to a far greater extent. However, there many counter arguments to this construct, such as the landscape wanderers enter in is always seemingly bigger than the planets in the sky, the extreme variations still occur in the same landscape that a wanderer no clips in, and the cohesive dark theme the environment always follows.

The Cognition Proposal
This theory suggests that everything in Level 24 is up to the wanderer's interpretation, similarly to Bohr's proposal regarding quantum physics. Level 24 could be all of the above, or none of the above. Everything is simply a reaction of the human psyche.

Dreamscape 2

Thats it, I'm done for. No one is coming to help me.
> Entrances and Exits
Entrances
Main entrance: no-clipping through the ceiling from Level 23.
Random no-clippage
It is rumored that one may no clip from Level 229.
Staring at the night sky while floating on the Ominous Ocean of Level 603 for 15 minutes might send one here.
Exits
Main exit: Although rare, wormholes may randomly appear, and entering any one of them will take you to Level 25. Do not enter black holes, however, as these will rip you apart.
No-clipping through glitching sections of the level. Theories suggest that one may no-clip to Level 15 when going through the glitching walls of Situation 25.
Random no-clippage.
