»⠀Moderate Entity Count
Description
46fullresolution

A current image of one of Level 46's ruins taken during the day by a B.R.L.A photographer.
46fullresolution

Level 46, often known as "The Arabian Desert" or "Empty Quarter," is a vast, boundless expanse of desert reminiscence of the Arabian desert—one of the immense and harshest deserts in The Frontrooms. The level's size remains undetermined, and the attempts to prove the presumption have been ambiguous due to the hazardous circumstances. Some argued that the barren landscape would change as one moved further from the entrance, while others believed the levels could be infinitely large. The desolate desert resembles a wasteland with irregular and intricately patterned golden sand, forming enormous dunes that can reach impressive heights. In response to wind sculpting, dunes may develop mesmerizing terrain with ridges and valleys. When climbing or navigating steep dune slopes, dunes can be unsteady alongside unstable dunes and collapse, burying or retaining individuals.

The level's diurnal cycle materializes out of sync with what happens in The Frontrooms; exhibiting an inconsistent time process via both days and nights that doesn't follow the predictable pattern and encompasses additionally prolonged periods, meandering from more than 48 hours to up to a week. Afternoon temperatures exceeding 120°F (49°C) provide an arid and drastic climate that could be lethal to human life. But nighttime temperatures often fall below zero, signaling a significant drop to -30 degrees Celsius, leading to hypothermia if one is not well equipped. Sunrise and sunset are the most convenient times to navigate, as the temperature is between 50°F and 80°F (10°C and 27°C) or lower inferior. Level 46 displays intermittent and unpredictable precipitation, resulting in stagnant puddles in shaded areas next to vegetation. Even so, these moisture sources usually remain contaminated by the Hydrolitis Plague, rendering them unreliable and unfit for human consumption.

Pic1

An image of Level 46's empty landscape nearby M.E.G. outpost taken by one of the M.E.G explorers.
Pic1

The atmosphere of Level 46 distinguishes itself with unobstructed scenery and intense sunlight during the day, with minimal sky coloring hues due to its scarcity of consequential greenery. Clouds are relatively infrequent due to the grinding environment and are often associated with specific weather conditions, such as the possibility of rainfall. The twilight skies tend to be unambiguous, making it an immaculate establishment for those curious about stargazing and astronomy. Studies and investigations reveal that this desert-like terra boasts three manifest celestial bodies, named Luna, Titan, and Europa, with the latter observable wrapped in a striking blue and green shade concealed among other starlights. Starlights and celestial bodies are apparent with outstanding clarity. Each night view features star patterns that are unevenly shifting. Many individuals declare that Level 46 starlight has an advantageous impact on one's sanity in a scientific, unproven manner.

Should one bury into the foundation or utilize a metal detector, they could stumble upon considerable antique yet intriguing objects underneath the ground. Coins, necklaces, containers, axes, metal bars, clothes, and other specialties that might qualify as intimate belongings—many suppositions propose multiple little metal bars cut into fragments, perhaps performing as coinage. B.R.L.A. is now seeking arbitrary locations encircling their outpost to offer and examine for further acquaintance concerning prospective bygone communities, considering the unclear origins of countless things buried in the dunes. The ruins discovered within the level further reinforce the widely accepted assumption that Level 46 was formerly an aspect of an ancient civilization.

Desert4001

A video of the desert before the sandstorm arrived.
Desert4001

When the sun rises, the ground coating rapidly heats up, concocting thermal disparities between the surface and the air above, compelling amiable air upwards. Muscular currents and turbulence in the outermost layer may pick up unconsolidated sand particles as this warm air inflates, eventually generating sandstorms. Dry sand and dust particles from the desert floor will blow into the ambiance at accelerations altering from 25 miles per hour (40 kilometers) to 50 miles per hour (80 kilometers) or more.

As the winds haul sand particles, treacherous circumstances emerge, and the sandstorms persist. Sandstorms dramatically impair visibility, making it difficult to maneuver and explore. As an outcome of the gravel air, one's eyes may get clouded, irritated, and painful. Inhaling fine sand and dust grains can affect an individual's health. It may worsen respiratory diseases, irritate the throat, induce coughing, and result in long-term health issues.

The desert is mainly known for its dry and harsh characteristics. However, in Level 46, vegetation has adapted to the extremely arid conditions and thrives in this challenging environment. Resistant species like acacia trees, date palms, and drought-tolerant cultivated shrubs can materialize around aquatic oases. Other plant life and flora are naturally scarce and restricted to positions with abundant water.

These plants, like saltbush, desert needle grass, and sand couch grass, can thrive in somewhat wetter environments and are well-suited for deserts with salty soil due to their adaptations. Several of the aforementioned plant species may be worthwhile in desperate or necessary situations, serving as vital supplies of nutrition and vibrancy like date palms, or they may present materials for manufacturing handicrafts and building shelters.

Oases
Level 46 has been known for hosting five oases strewn around the landscape; the oases, notably the one in The Frontrooms, represent comparatively tiny agricultural regions replenished with water for inhabitants, taking the form of a natural spring or subsurface aquifer. Their thick forested foliage and the presence of ample water distinguish them from the surrounding desert landscape. These areas not only support plant growth but also provide nearby shelter and a variety of food and water sources for sustenance.

According to inquiries into the water's source, those may emerge as a minimal lake or pool following a prolonged downpour or as a natural spring erupting upwards from the subsurface. The mere presence of water is essential to allowing an oasis to thrive in the harsh, arid desert habitat. The vast and endless desert terrain makes it unlikely for people to find oases, which are vital hubs in the harsh desert conditions, offering nourishment and relief from the obstacles.

Each of the five oases in Level 46 has the following names: Desert's Mirage, Life's Spring, Night's Haven, Enchanted Spring, and Water's Edge. Those peculiar, still-unknown qualities are yet to reveal themselves, including keeping entities from infiltrating the zone, prohibiting natural disasters from occurring there and being exhaustively complimentary of catastrophes. Although further research and breakdown into the abnormal feature fail to uncover any information of interest, this location seems blessed with its remarkable possessions.

The remnants of magnesium sulfate (Epsom salt) and other inexplicable substances have been detected in Level 46's oasis water, showing that they are indistinguishable compared to Level 37 lukewarm water. While the oasis's spring water is pleasantly frigid and appropriate for the desert's summer weather, further inspection discloses that Level 46's water composition and unknown constituents differ from those in Level 37. This research determination led to the belief that the level's unidentified compounds correspond to the oasis's incognito traits.

The following is a list of five oases located on Level 46.

Desert's Mirage: The first prominent oasis on Level 46 is called Desert's Mirage. Due to being the one that many individuals overlook, B.R.L.A. established a community there. The outpost's status as an oasis and its immediate water reserve made it feasible to develop agriculture that generated food-producing plants and fruits.
Life's Spring - The Life's Spring oasis lies 95.59 kilometers south of the M.E.G. base outpost. The oases have several ancient dwellings, farms, and other buildings excavated near an oasis, exhibiting indications of an old occupancy of people from decades ago. The oases also display historical signals of what used to be human civilizations and the production of crops around oasis regions.
Night's Haven - The Night's Haven oasis distinguishes itself from the rest of the four oases due to its unconventional and distinctive markers. The sky's intention gradually turns nighty as one approaches the oasis, notwithstanding the duration of the level. The time cycle in Night's Heaven perpetually stays the same even though the oasis mood temperature will warm in disparity to the ordinary level's nighttime temperature.
Enchanted Spring - The Enchanted Spring oasis includes springs comparable to other oases, but the water appears neon and illuminates its own. Under a thorough examination, the water in this oasis is composed of Corruptocolor—also known as Substum Insolor—a neon liquid associated with Corruptionite.
Water's Edge - The most recently found oasis on Level 46 is Water's Edge. The oasis' existence is assured; it lies significantly outlying away from the M.E.G. outpost, retaining the anticipation of a standard oasis but more extensive than the other mentioned oasis. Many assert that after one desires to continue farther beyond the oasis in one route.
Due to its unrestricted size, Level 46 could incorporate more than the five oases stated previously. Several individuals proclaimed to have found more oases but were still uncertain. All conclude that those declarations are likely to be Water's Edge due to its large proportions that can arise in various shapes and regions. M.E.G. and B.R.L.A. are now conducting research, searching for further data, and verifying the validity of a finding claim.

Temple Scrolls
Level46

An image taken inside the Temple Scroll corridor by a M.E.G. photographer.
Level46

The Ancient One, a long-gone civilization that attained Level 46, constructed the grandest ruined site known as Temple Scrolls, a long-gone civilization that attained Level 46. The building's architecture and design are equivalent to those of Egyptian temples. Nevertheless, there is no manifestation on-site or documented record that the temple is an establishment of worship or rituals. Instead, the temple's prominent purpose is to gather precious artifacts like sculptures and paintings, accompanying a collection of multiple valuable objects and articles. Extensive, towering gates marked the entrances of temples adorned with artistic reliefs and the civilization's language. The sweeping courtyards seen in temples are likely to have been employed for gatherings and discussions. The interior incorporates a labyrinth of passages and hallways that resemble a maze, ostensibly meant to mislead invaders and safeguard the temple's resources.

The chambers within the structure are enormous and supported by several columns, with exquisite carvings, paintings, and linguistic characters decorating the walls. The temple wall inscriptions matched the astronomical and geographical features of Level 46. They offered details about events like the movement of stars, forecasts for rain and daylight patterns, and a map of the nearby land. This information, based on a detailed analysis of the inscriptions, also included directions to other settlements. Furthermore, the record uses a mathematical formula comparable to The Frontrooms and computes the ordinances of Level 46's physics. M.E.G. has a station set up afterward to the temple, manipulates the temple as its headquarters of operations, and conducts breakdowns both within and outside the temple.

The Ancient One
The name "The Ancient Ones" refers to the now probably extinct civilization that formerly inhabited Level 46 and has been speculated to be the origin of the many aberrant ruins. The headwaters of their demise are unknown. It is probable that a phenomenon known as "The Flicker" led to The Ancient Ones' disappearance and the abandonment of their structures. Although plenty of wax tablets and papyrus writing discovered on Level 370 show that The Ancient One relocated there after the occurrence and established a new association there, it is still undefined where they have proceeded or where they live because the community does not exist till this day. What is clear is that The Ancient Ones possessed a degree of scientific development sufficient to provide astral charts and a solar cycle forecast that are relatively more accurate and comprehensive than those assembled by the M.E.G.

Entities
Facelings and Hounds are the exclusive entities at Level 46, predominantly appearing at night or during a sandstorm. Although several people declare to have seen creatures emerge from the dune, it generally seems that they are not identical to the usual entities in The Backrooms, as they are considerably more aggressive than regular and lack any symptoms of vulnerability. This level's Hounds and Facelings are sentient sand in the constitution of their entities, with the sand conducting to form into the bodies and flesh of the entities. Nevertheless, exerting sufficient pressure on one of the entities—such as a punch or kick—triggers the sand to lose its anomalous properties, causing it to lose its body parts of bodies or die. M.E.G. attempts to study the entities on this level but fails since when entities perish, their bodies shift and pour into the sand floor.

Colonies and Outposts
B7D2AAA4-0F96-47A4-ACEB-9CD8FBA473AC

A failed attempt to build a campfire in Level 46.
B7D2AAA4-0F96-47A4-ACEB-9CD8FBA473AC

B.R.L.A. Mirage outpost
The Desert Mirage Oasis, an outpost established by the Backrooms Living Association (B.R.L.A.), serves as a sanctuary for travelers. The outpost accommodates 55-63 individuals, including 27 permanent residents, and is a self-sufficient village constructed with wooden cabins made from wood imported from other levels. The outpost features amenities such as wifi, solar-powered electricity, and running water. The B.R.L.A. offers essential resources and support to those who continue their journey through the backrooms.

M.E.G. outposts "Desert Rose"
The Major Explorer Group (M.E.G.) has strategically placed outposts near modern-looking ruins and Temple Scroll, the purpose of which is to be related to the containment of valuable and ancient objects and items inside the temple and investigate and study unknown behind The Ancient Ones. Each outpost shelters a small number of individuals, typically between 8-20 people. The outpost will politely request that travelers vacate and provide directions to the B.R.L.A. Mirage outpost if one persists for an extended period. M.E.G. members will escort travelers to the designated outpost upon request.

Recovered Paper
The gods lied to us. There is no salvation. There is no afterlife. There is no hope beyond the void. There is no ascension from the chasm. Entropy is the only freedom we have, and we must embrace it. Millennium from now, nothingness shall prevail. Decay shall once again regain its autarch status under its primordial dominion. The only savior we have is the opening arms of time, which will inevitably bring everything to an ultimate collapse, where afterward, only the lost spirits of the damned will roam the endless darkness that comes afterward.

Entropia gloria!
Entrances and Exits
Level46-3

Another image of Level 46's desert dune.
Level46-3

Entrances
Find a gateway composed of sandstone on Level 21.
Dry areas in Level 45 may lead one to this level.
Wasteland In Level 50 may slowly gradient into this level.
Jumping into a window displaying a scorching, hot desert in Level 2.1 will lead one to this level.
Sailing on a canoe westward in Level 301 can take you to this level.
There is a maintenance hatch in the Surveillance Hub on Level 326 that leads directly to here.
Exits
Did you know that purposely no-clipping into the ground for this level may lead one to Level 47?
Passing out due to heat exhaustion and falling to the ground has a high chance of no-clipping into Level 10.7.
No-clipping into one of the modern-day-looking ruins may lead one to Level 1 or Level 22.
No-clipping oneself in the water of the oasis named Enchanted Spring will lead one to Level 37.
A person may suddenly appear in Level 671 without notice of the move.
Attempt self-burial to enter Level 207.
Extremely rarely, wandering for long enough may lead one to Level 606. However, this is impossible at the lower-gravity areas of the level.
Finding a mono-yellow colored stone will take one to Level 0.
Drinking Liquid Pain brings one to Level 426.
Jumping into a pit of black sand sends one to Level 603.
No-clipping into an incredibly rare pool of blood sends one to Level 665.
No-clipping or fainting in an oasis will teleport you to Level 301.

Thestairsbetween

What if I told you that this is an image of Level 47?
Thestairsbetween

Description
Did you know that Level 47 has an anomalous property that converts any information pertaining to it into a question? Isn't it strange that one is unable to write any information about the level without it being in the form of a question, while the writer does not appear to notice? Wouldn't one conclude that Level 47 presents a serious memetic hazard and a potential leak of hazardous and anomalous information?

Beside this, did you know that the physical characteristics of the level are superfluous to mention and quite redundant? What if I told you that Level 47 consists of an extensive set of white drywall rooms, interconnected by randomly placed doorways, half-walls, and stairwells leading to nowhere in particular? Have you noticed that linear space is distorted in the level, making it virtually impossible to exactly navigate, or even return to one's previous position? Did you know that the cause of the anomalous memetic properties of this level is unknown, as the level itself does not appear to differ greatly from other levels?

Colonies and Outposts
Are there any colonies or outposts on this level?

Addendum
Kauer Research Organization
The following text documents an exploration of Level 47 carried out by Kauer Researcher Bennett, and operated by Exploration Captain Holden, transcribed verbatim.

<BEGIN LOG>

Researcher Bennett: Where the hell am I? Didn’t you say I would end up in-

Captain Holden: Bennett, is everything alright? Where are you? You’re off our radar.

Researcher Bennett: Can you hear me? Hold on.
(small pause as Researcher Bennett presumably adjusts his receiver)
Alright, how do I sound, Captain?

Captain Holden: We hear you loud and clear, Bennett. Can you describe your surroundings?

Researcher Bennett: Uh, well, have you ever seen those empty houses, before they’re furnished? Can you picture that, with a sort-of dreamlike feel to it?

Captain Holden: Strange.
(off to the side): Do we have an environment like this logged in the database?

Researcher Bennett: (pause) Captain?

Captain Holden: We’re trying to locate you. (murmuring)
It doesn’t look like we know where you are. Is there anything near you that sticks out to you?

Researcher Bennett: Haven’t I already said that it’s empty?

Captain Holden: No need to get agitated, Bennett; I understand you’re phased.

Researcher Bennett: Did I seem agitated?
(shouts): Is anyone there?

Captain Holden: Is everything alright?

Researcher Bennett: Isn’t this place strange?

Captain Holden: Well, I can’t see what you’re seeing. Can you describe its architecture?

Researcher Bennett: “Basic” would be an overstatement, wouldn’t it? I’ve already said that it’s like an empty house, yeah? Would it make sense if I said that there are staircases going upward that lead to nowhere, with connecting rooms containing similar oddities, Captain?

Captain Holden: I… Yes, I believe that would make sense. Are you feeling alright, Bennett?

Researcher Bennett: Can you please hurry up, sir? Can’t you tell I’m not exactly enjoying myself here — wherever I am?

Captain Holden: We’re doing the best we can. (murmuring) Just hold on.

Researcher Bennett: (quietly, presumably to self): Freaky, don’t you think?

Captain Holden: Something is off.
(indecipherable conversation) …Yes, exactly. It’s not right.
Alright, Bennett, can you hear me?

Researcher Bennett: Loud and clear, Captain.

Captain Holden: I’d like to ask you a couple questions.

Researcher Bennett: Yeah, that’s okay. Why?

Captain Holden: A simple hunch; now: What is your name?

Researcher Bennett: (pause) Bennett, sir; Researcher Bennett. May I question the intent of this?

Captain Holden: (quietly, presumably to self) Alright, noted.
Now, can you describe your current surroundings?

Researcher Bennett: I already answered that question.

Captain Holden: …Interesting. (pause)
(quietly, presumably writing) Does… not… apply… (indecipherable)

Researcher Bennett: Can you tell me what this is about?

Captain Holden: Bennett, I ask that you answer the question for research purposes.

Researcher Bennett: Roger that, Captain. I've said that the environment appears to be empty and unfurnished, with no remarkable features aside from the occasional staircase, yeah? Have I added that it smells vaguely of… lime?

Captain Holden: Bennett, can you describe the environment in the form of a statement, and not as an inquiry?

Researcher Bennett: Is that… not what I’ve been doing?

Captain Holden: (pause) How about that.

<END LOG>

Level 48 is the 49th level of the Backrooms.
General Overview
Dontchicagotothebackrooms

A popular image of Level 48.
Dontchicagotothebackrooms

Level 48, informally known as "Piercing the Clouds" or "Skyscrapers of the Fog," is an indefinite expanse of stratus clouds dotted with skyscrapers. The level's low gravity allows wanderers to float throughout the level, flapping their arms like wings to ascend. The level maintains a relatively chilly temperature. A gentle breeze constantly flows through Level 48, contributing to the feeling of weightlessness and a misty atmosphere, akin to the mist exerted by an air purifier. Periodically, the sky shifts like a gradient, from light blue to orange to navy blue.

An invisible barrier nestles underneath the dense fog in the lower areas of Level 48, preventing wanderers and other sentient beings from interacting with whatever lies below. Before approaching the barrier, one will see their surroundings take on a reddish hue for a few seconds, followed by a powerful gust of wind to blow them back up to skyscraper height. Imagery taken near the barrier is corrupted and unreadable, primarily displaying static, yet audio from recordings remains intact.

Yeahchicagotothebackrooms

Another image of Level 48.
Yeahchicagotothebackrooms

It is impossible to enter the buildings, as they contain impenetrable glass and steel. The skyscraper windows reveal luxury apartments, modern offices, hotel suites, observation decks, indoor pools, and restaurants. On the balconies and rooftops of the buildings, one may find regenerative supply crates, MREs, and Almond Water bottles, providing a constant supply of beneficial items for wanderers. These items lose their regenerative properties outside of Level 48.

The skyscrapers light up when night falls, boasting a plethora of colors. Foglights may also appear below the clouds, emitting various colors and luminosities. Despite the skyscrapers' light pollution, dark skies are dotted with thousands of stars. Some skyscrapers emit a blinding light beacon through a large prism attached to their roofs, launching wanderers upward as they approach close.

While gazing at Level 48's sky, wanderers may witness far-away aircraft, planets, floating islands, meteor showers, and mythical creatures, such as dragons. Distant sounds like draconic roars, jet engines, and asteroid booms emanate from these sights. As one views these mythic sights, one will feel compelled to fly towards them, soaring high above the skyscrapers.

Speakers ranging in size and loudness sit on the balconies and roofs of some skyscrapers. These speakers play the music currently playing in the background of this document. A control panel allows them to change the tracks or turn the speakers off, but it will return to the default music shortly after. The speakers are indestructible.

Entities
SSS (Sky Strolling Slimes)
Fargoscargomod

The Sky Strolling Slimes, colloquially referred to as SSS or Triple S Entities, are Cnidarian entities exclusive to Level 48. They resemble slimes or jellyfish, levitating freely in the level's skies. They appear during the day and mysteriously vanish at dark.

SSS is harmless to wanderers as they cannot sting or bite other biological lifeforms. They levitate and roam randomly, sometimes in droves, with hundreds of other SSSs. When an SSS randomly strikes a solid surface, such as a skyscraper or a wanderer, it will rapidly eject itself off the object, except on some balconies and rooftops, where it rests before taking flight. When staying in a specific spot long enough, they secrete a slimy substance that may cause wanderers to slip over. During significant wind events, SSS tends to move against the wind's direction, often clinging near a skyscraper to minimize wind shear. The entity sports a transparent body. Their blood is transparent and slimy, resembling sludge. Their size ranges from 15 to 35 centimeters (5.9 to 13.7 inches). An SSS's lifespan ranges from five days to three weeks.

Human Settlements
The Rooftop Union
Founded in September of 2023, The Rooftop Union is a collaborative settlement within Level 48, consisting of scientists from the Major Explorer Group, Backroom Colonists, Entity Research Committee, and the Spatial Exploration Organization. They study the level's various anomalies, from its low gravity, invisible barrier, the SSS, and many more. They are secluded from outsiders unless they are a scientist from one of the four mentioned groups. The Rooftop Union boasts a stable population of 91.

Description
Level !+!

An image of Level 49 in its regular state.
Level !+!

Level 49, otherwise known as "Intrusive Thoughts", is an expansive hospital corridor consisting of gloomy lights, hospital stretchers, patient monitors, wheelchairs, and other hospital-like objects. The level is mainly shrouded in darkness due to the lack of lighting; the lights appear to be weak, as they do not significantly light up the level. Because of this, wanderers should be careful of any tripping hazards.

Entities will not attack wanderers if they stay within the light. However, traversing into the darkness will cause wanderers to become a defenseless prey towards the entities. If an entity spots a wanderer while being exposed to the light, it will calmly stare until the wanderer steps out. It has been recorded that these entities will wait for days just to attack their victims.

On occasions, doors leading to rooms can be found; these rooms usually can be medical-surgical patient rooms, examination rooms, and other hospital-like rooms. However, on rare chances, one can find a room that does not relate to a hospital. These include interrogation rooms, hotel lobbies, and more.

A unique property of the level that should be noted is that depending on your thoughts the level will change into a different state; for example, feeling a sense of anger will cause the level to form into a red hallway. Each state is temporary and will last for a couple of hours before returning to its regular state. The following list shows every documented state that has been discovered.

Angry Thoughts
Thinking of angry thoughts will cause the level to form into a red hospital while entities will burst out of doors and begin searching for wanderers. Entering the rooms and hiding under a bed will usually leave you alive until the state wears off.

Depressing Thoughts
Thinking of depressing thoughts will lead the level to form into a depressing-like hospital with heartbeat monitors blaring out a long beep from some of the rooms. During this state, ghost-like entities will rise and begin searching for wanderers.

Joyful Thoughts
Thinking of joyful thoughts will cause the level to form into a happy-like hospital with positive messages written on paper being pinned onto the wall. Wanderers can find items that gives a sensation of happiness during this state; these object can be anything as it depends on what the wanderer who discovers the object likes.

Nyctophobic Thoughts
Thinking of nyctophobic or thoughts about the dark will cause every power source within the level to shut off, along with light sources to malfunction. During this state, any sort of light will be absorbed. The only exceptions are the illuminated faces of Smilers.

Claustrophobic Thoughts
Thinking of claustrophobic thoughts will lead the level to slowly become narrow until it has reached the point where wanderers will suffocate. Very few have survived from this state, as it is incredibly difficult to survive.

Thalassophobic Thoughts
Thinking of thalassophobic thoughts will cause the level to quickly flood. There have been several reports of The Thing on Level 7 swimming in the waters and chasing down wanderers only to suddenly fade away on near impact. This is most likely a hallucination but cannot be confirmed yet.

Nostalgic Thoughts
Level 250

An image of the photographers "home".
Level 250

Thinking of nostalgic thoughts will cause the level to fade into your home back in the The Frontrooms. If you did not have a home back in The Frontrooms, the level will fade into a structure you consider "memorable". Because of this property, this state varies from each person's perspective. Strangely, your "home" stretches for miles, acting as if it were a labyrinth. Several objects wanderers will find familiar with are present; these objects give a sense of nostalgia to the person experiencing this state.

Entities
One thing that should be noted about Level 49 is that the entities appear to be fused with other entities. For example, a combination of both Smilers and Skin-Stealers can be seen throughout the level. Entities will always appear in each state, except for one, that being the thalassophobic state. Any encounters with entities during the thalassophobic state are assumed to be hallucinations.

Colonies and Outposts
Anomalously, the level creates copies for each wanderer who ends up on Level 49. Interestingly, another wanderer may be able to enter another wanderer's copy. However, this would cause the level to be heavily unstable, as the level cannot handle more than two wanderers thinking of different thoughts.

Entrances and Exits
Entrances
Entering an out-of-place hospital corridor on Fragmented Recollections will lead you here.
Opening an unlocked door labeled “Intrusive Thoughts” on A Long Forgotten Exclamation will take you here.
Finding a hospital submerged underwater and entering it on Level 7 will bring you here.
Several reports state that the level could be entered through Level 14.
Smashing a car's window in Level 220 sends one here.
Exits
Finding a door with the inscription "Room 420" on the door will take you to Level 420. However, this exit remains unconfirmed.
Opening and entering a heavily damaged door will bring you to Level 14.

I continue to move down the interminable trail as thirst and starvation gradually set in. In the middle of a sweltering desert, my body is exhausted. I start to run out of vitality and stroll. Level 50, also known as "The Moribund Highway", is the current 51st level found in the Backrooms.

Description
Level50-1

The first known image of Level 50.
Level50-1

Level 50 is a seemingly infinite paved asphalt two-lane highway amid desert terrain, with the street stretching in both directions and indefinitely fading into the distance fog. Every step makes a little echo that adds to the impression of solitude, and the sound of the air blowing across the route slowly coating it with dust and sand. Every stride forward feels like a loop back in on itself, as no one knows what lies beyond. The path intersects once it has traveled a decent distance—around every mile or when the ascending path cannot continue in a straight line. The pathway is also known for having a non-euclidean temperament, which makes it exceedingly difficult to navigate or localize the level. Some intersections or roads themselves loop back to the beginning of the route, forcing wanderers to change lanes.

The highway lies in a frigid desert basin that lengthened much beyond the size of the actual route. As a representation of a wasteland, it has irregularly and elaborately flattened sands, as well as a mountain range that can be seen nearby from a great distance away. The descriptive information for the mountains is sparse since they frequently have hazardous environments and are demanding to scale. Except for the road and an electric pole that serves no use, there isn't much human infrastructure in the region. Plant life resembles that found in front rooms, including brittlebush, sagebrush, cologne, and other species. However, if one were to turn off the road, the desert would grow more arid and plantless, and the environment would become more hazardous.

Level50-2

Another image of Level 50.
Level50-2

Numerous vehicles without license plates rarely appear on the road. Numerous of them seem to be in a condition of time halting, and none are accurately parked as if time were to stop while they were moving. Although virtually all cars are locked, it is necessary to note that it is still feasible to get into them. Supplies and other necessities for survival are known to be inside. Traveling by vehicle becomes difficult at this level since the automobile may suffer damage and run out of gasoline due to long-term abandonment. Function cars can ease and smooth out a journey for the traveler regardless of whether it depends on luck, offer cover from the scorching air and brisk breeze, and serve as a place to rest while traveling.

The terrain is illuminated by constant light during the day without a cycle. Anyone present at this level will experience a variety of atmospheric conditions. The most common circumstance is sunny weather, which can raise temperatures to 38°C (simply over 100°F). Because of this, it is advised to stay on the path and in an operational vehicle. Almond water is also highly suggested due to the high temperature. The additional condition is foggy when the entire landscape is covered in fog that limits the range of vision. Although this state can cause the temperature to drop, it typically brings on a strong breeze that might nearly result in a storm.

Level50-3

Level 50 in the cloudy condition.
Level50-3

Although the highway path is non-euclidean, there is a greater likelihood that you will come across other wanderers on your journey. Additionally, due to the heat and terrible weather, the bodies and bones of people can be found decomposing by the side of the road with the flesh torn off the bone. The idea of meeting and traveling with other wanderers may sound great, but the hazards of this level come from the stray people that walk the highway. Many unfortunate travelers tend to be hijacked and robbed while moving, with the hijackers often pointing out the car that the traveler is driving. Although individuals are rarely killed during robberies, victims sometimes die from a lack of livelihood supplies due to harsh weather or from wounds and blood loss during the fighting.

Much of this level remains unexplored, as there is only one way out. If one travels far enough, one could find a way out of this level by taking a route that leads to a petrol station amid the desert. The gas station and empty parking lots are in an abandoned state. Goods and supplies in gas station stores are frequently worthless and rotting owing to their perfect condition, leaving just a few items, including tinned food, batteries, flashlights, a crowbar, a bulletproof vest, and more. The exit is located in the back of the store and will take you to Level 51. In addition to having a single exit, one source reportedly claimed to have discovered a highway exit that appeared to go on for miles. Because the individual did not delve inside it, it is unknown what waits at the end, assuming one exists.

Log 2472
Radio Transmission, Log ID: 2472

The following is a radio transmission between an explorer name "Fritz Smith" and another explorer codename: “Ranger”
Open Log 2472 >

Entities
There are few entities in Level 50 that are frequently seen in the desert further on. Even if the entities aren't the most dangerous thing on this level, it's still not an ideal choice to wander around the wasteland, especially when it's cloudy, because anything may be concealing inside the dense fog. Hounds and Skin-Stealers are the two currently known entities on Level 50.

Colonies And Outposts
There are no known colonies or outposts on this level.

Entrances and Exits
Entrances
Level 50 may be accessed from Level 79 by escaping through a fire escape. Via Noclip, it is possible to enter from Level 22. Another way to access Level 50 is through riding an escalator sporting a centered couble continuous yellow line found on the roadways of this level.

Exits
Level 50 may be departed through the door in the gas station store, which leads to Level 51. Another exit is to seamlessly wander through the route until it slowly transitions to Level 41. The level may suddenly turn to a state of dusk. This may be a sign one is about to enter Level -69. Besides, going far on both sides of the road in Level 50 will lead you to Level 224.

entries.name: Alternates
entries.content:
The Alternates are sinister and enigmatic beings. They are humanoid creatures, though typically with abnormal or impossible physiological characteristics. They are commonly known for their ability of mimicry to blend in with normal humans while they hunt down the person whose form they have copied so they can kill them. Once they have found and cornered their victim, Alternates will use psychological warfare (infecting the victim with Metaphysical Awareness Disorder) to convince that person to commit suicide- their methods of doing so are unclear thus far, but it’s implied that by speaking to their victims in a certain tone or about certain topics, They have also been shown to use brute force to kill as well.
Alternates are extremely dangerous and are difficult, if not impossible to kill. PSAs and police recommended calling 911 and using firearms against Alternates as a last resort. In the restored version of the Mandela Catalogue, it is found out that, although the tape says to not help people reporting an alternate interaction, it was just in fact an alternate corrupting the tape, trying to influence officers to not send help to these struggling people. Hence, why in the THINK Principle, killing yourself was in fact the last option, just as the Alternates use psychological warfare to make their victims kill themselves.
Alternates have existed for at least thousands of years, dating as far back as the beginning of the Biblical Era. The earliest known Alternate was the one posing as Archangel Gabriel, who foretold the coming of the Savior, Jesus Christ.
In Vol. 4, it was implied that Adam, the first man, was replaced or turned into the 'original alternate' shortly after the world was created.
In Exhibition, it was implied that in the ancient times, when the Elohim decided to flood the world for unknown reasons, a false angel who pretended to be Archangel Gabriel tried to stop Noah from building an ark. However, Noah refused to obey his command and built the ark. Out of its rage, the false angel would then secretly leave a creature on the ark, resulting in Noah's death. This creature was implied to a Alternate.
For thousands of years, the Alternates had been hiding in the shadows. When the true Gabriel was sent to Bethlehem, Israel to announce that the Messiah would soon be born, the Alternate "Gabriel" replaced him and sabotaged the Annunciation. It was heavily implied that a Alternate took the true Messiah's role in history.
During the Analog Era, the Alternates became more active than usual. Their actions resulted in deaths of many humans. However, after stepping into Digital Era, people started to believe that the Alternates had already been exterminated. However, evidence shows that, in fact, many Alternates still lived on Earth, presumably waiting for the best chance to strike. Their next step is still unknown.
It has been implied that the United States Department of Temporal Phenomena possesses several Alternates in "custody"/captivity for research and studying as MCPD actively search for them and put out flyers for them.
Types
Type One: Doppelgänger
Perfect or near identical copies of someone. They are almost, if not completely impossible to differentiate from the original. An example of this type are the Doppelgängers seen in Vol. 1, the first Alternate example shown in the remake of said volume, and the "Completed Assimilation" shown in Interlude.
Type Two: Unspeakable
Previously known as "Detectable", Unspeakables are the second category of alternate in which Alternate Gabriel belongs to, so far being the only one in this category. Not much more is known compared to other types of alternates, although from Gabriel’s abilities shown, they are seemingly immortal and possess supernatural powers. Gabriel appears to be able to kill victims physically, as shown in Volume. 4 when Dave is killed.
Type Three: Flawed Impersonators/Overdriven Assimilations
Extremely flawed copies of their original counterpart, possessing missing or exaggerated features such as extremely long limbs, faceless heads, or even having entirely upside-down anatomy. Examples of this type are N, Faceless Girl, The Preacher, & Alternate Cesar.
Type Four: Tulpa
Alternates willed into existence by the imagination of an individual, mainly children. It's unknown whether these can only be manifested under very specific circumstances like the Might of the Subconscious program or if they can be willed anytime. It's thought that they might manifest through TVs and Mirrors. An example of this type is the Murray's Alternate.
Powers & Abilities
General
Shapeshifting: Alternates can shapeshift into other lifeforms, usually humans but also animals as shown in Vol. 2. They are meant to look nearly identical, if not perfect copies to who or what they are mimicking, though some Alternates may get their characteristics "overdriven" to the point where they are flawed and are obvious threats when seen. Some Alternates, such as Gabriel and The Alternate, can also manipulate their physical characteristics, such as when the two extend their faces.
Voice/Audio Mimicry: Alternates can mimic the voices, music, and radio audio of others to trick people.
Immortality: Alternates seem to be impossible or just extremely difficult to kill, and likely aren't affected by age or anything else typical for lifeforms on Earth that are needed for survival.
Insanity & Suicide Inducement: Alternates are known for inducing M.A.D. (Metaphysical Awareness Disorder) onto their victims.
Flight: Some Alternates seem to have the ability to fly/float, shown with The Alternate in Vol. 333 and Alternate Gabriel considering he was masquerading as an angel. It is unknown if this is exclusively for those Alternates or them all.
Teleportation/Spectrum Travelling: Alternates can seemingly teleport to stalk their next victims.
Demon Physiology: It is heavily implied that Alternates are actually demons.
Tulpa's
Imagination Manipulation: Tulpa Alternates can manifest through the imagination of others.
Mirror Teleportation: From this, they can travel through reflective surfaces and TV.
Unspeakable's
The abilities of Alternate Gabriel, an Unspeakable Alternate, are unknown, though he is likely and heavily implied to be the one responsible for bringing the Alternates to Earth to terrorize humans, which may be an ability for this type.

entries.name: Metaphysical Awareness Disorder
entries.content:
Metaphysical Awareness Disorder, otherwise known as M.A.D is a psychological/mental illness brought upon by Alternates giving humans verbal information that is not desired to be known by them. After being given this information, the main symptoms of this disorder manifest, which consist of:
Going insane, or hence mad
Extreme desire to kill yourself/commit suicide
Becoming delusional & paranoid
There has been a 95% increase of diagnosis of this disorder in the 3rd quarter of 1982, the current year of Volume 1. The death rate of M.A.D victims is currently 97%, 100% of these deaths by suicide. However, the remaining 3% of the M.A.D victims proves the effectiveness of the delusion reversal.
To avoid the development of M.A.D, one needs to:
Avoid excessively frequent religious practices
Avoid unnecessary beliefs in philosophical implications
Avoid opening their eyes when they are certain that the "man in the corner" is now inches away from their face. Watching.
Metaphysical Awareness Disorder is a fatal mental illness that has been making a certain return in recent months.
M.A.D is a result of exposure to verbal information that is not desired to be known. The rate of death by suicides patients diagnosed with M.A.D is 97%. But don't worry, the remaining 3% makes it worth trying to reverse the delusion.
Avoiding the root causes of Metaphysical Awareness Disorder development is the first step to being safe. First. Avoid excessively frequent religious practices. Avoid unnecessary beliefs in philosophical implications. Last but not least, looking after your loved ones is a key factor for maintaining mental stability.
Speculation
Metaphysical Awareness Disorder may have the side effect of changing the victim’s personality. This is possibly evidenced by Evelin’s quote (about Adam); “he used to be such a nice guy before he started doing those investigations with Jonah.”
As the name would imply MAD appears to have something to do with the nature of existence within the universe. So far many theories believe that the information in MAD is the knowledge of Gabriel and his actions.

entries.name: Humans
entries.content:
Adam is never described in the Bible, but there are various depictions of him that represents him as follow: a relatively tall and athletic man in his 20s with a white skin, black eyes, short straight or slightly curly hair that varies from dark to light brown and ,sometimes, a thick and unkempt beard.
In the Mandela Catalogue
In the Beginners' Bible/Vol. 2
In the brief appearance that Adam does in The Mandela Catalogue Vol. 2 and in the sample-episode of the Beginners' Bible, Adam is depicted as a short man in his late teens with a white skin, and skinny body, slightly curly brown hair, black eyes, thin and curved eyebrows, round face, French nose and a normally-sized circular ears.
Adam Murray
Adam Murray is the secondary protagonist of The Mandela Catalogue, serving as the secondary protagonist of Act 1, and one of the two main protagonists in Act 2 (alongside Thatcher Davis).
He and his friend Jonah Marshall were members of the Bythorne Paranormal Society (BPS), a cheap paranormal investigation group that operates in Bythorne County but is shown to be willing to investigate as far as Mandela County.
Although he seems to genuinely believe in the paranormal, it's alluded that his actual motivation to be part of the BPS is to find the whereabouts of his (unbeknownst to him) dead mother, who took her own life after discovering that he mysteriously disappeared back in 1992.
Alex Kister
Alex Kister is the creator of the analog horror series The Mandela Catalogue, on which this wiki project is based. He also created a digital horror series called Mystifying Oracle. He plays multiple characters in both of his series.
Cesar Torres
Cesar Torres has been replaced off-screen by an alternate after it managed to break into their home, breaking the window. Later that same day, the alternate would go on to disguise itself as Cesar in his signature prom suit and call Cesar's friend Mark Heathcliff. During the recorded phone call, the alternate describes as Cesar that he found his mom passed out after screaming and is on his way to the hospital, then asking Mark to turn on the security cameras at his house while he's gone. During the phone call, "Cesar"'s face glitches out to have a large smile, teasing Cesar's replacement.
Dave Lee
The Mandela Catalogue Vol.333
Dave was sent and asked to recover the footage from a collection of VHS tapes found by the MCPD. Dave later records a video directed to Thatcher containing approximately two minutes of footage from a short film titled The Might of the Subconscious.
The Mandela Catalogue Vol. 4
Dave gets a call from O'Brien, and he says he should consider getting a job at the church, which he initially turns down, while Evelin sorts through their old tapes, stealing one. Later on Dave finds out Evelin watched the tape, and fires her over the phone. After this, he calls O'Brien back and decides to take him up on his offer.
A while later, Dave calls Thatcher and tells him that he's decided to stop his business, tells him to let go of the missing persons cases, and tells him to find a new meaning in life.
After this, Dave goes to visit O'Brien, outside the church. All of a sudden the skies turn black, the wind stops blowing and Dave is in complete darkness. After a few seconds, Dave sees a light from the clouds, where O'Brien emerges, who turned out to be Gabriel the whole time. He then mocks him. Dave tries to reassure himself, trying to convince himself that Gabriel isn't real, and Gabriel then reveals that Dave has already done all his bidding for him. He then starts to laugh maniacally, with Dave falling down, presumably dying, bleeding from the eyes.
The aftermath of his encounter with Gabriel are shown in the form of a news report on his death in St. Gabriel Church. It's described that, prior to his death, a homeowner could hear his screaming at 12 A.M.
The report on Dave's death is suddenly interrupted by what seems to be an Intruder-induced corruption, first showing a man with a featureless face staring into the viewer prior to changing into what appears to be text reading gibberish over a white background. The text "No more running away" can be also briefly seen before the transmission returns to normal.
Dave's body was transported to the Bythorne Hospital morgue, where the two nurses performing the autopsy find out that both of his eyes are missing. Upon the discovery, one of the nurses opens his cranium, revealing his brain, which, according to various statements from Alex Kister, had exploded.
Evelin Miller
Evelin Miller is shown to be a very curious and polite young woman. Despite breaking up with her ex, Adam Murray, she still seems to care about him when she didn't hear from him for days. She's also shown to be capable of stealing material of Thatcher Davis and Dave Lee to appeal her curiosity.
Jonah Edmund Marshall
Jonah is a tan-skinned, tall-faced male with white dyed hair. He is seen wearing a dark jacket with a light-colored hood.
Jonah is a carefree, yet heavily anxious individual. When asked to be serious by Adam, Jonah often replies with some sort of joke, yet always put himself out of harms way such as staying in their car as Adam explored their client's house or fleeing the house without Adam at the end of The Mandela Catalogue Vol. 2.
Jesus Christ
Yeshua ben Yosef (lit. Joshua, son of Joseph), better known as Jesus Christ in the mythos of the religions which believe in him, was the founder of a monotheistic religion called Christianity. Yeshua was the son of Maria, who was the wife of Yoseph. Labbi Yeshua established the basis of Christianity. He created a sect called Nazarene within Judaism. His teachings and claims were viewed as heretic by many rabbis of some orthodox sects within Judaism. Followers of Yeshua created a new religion known as Christianity under the leadership of Kifas (also known as Simon Pedro, leader of the twelve disciples), who was the first Pàpà , after Labbi Yeshua left the earth. They began to spread Christianity under the leadership of Kifas. Believers of this religion believe that Labbi Yeshua is the son of God Yehweh, who is supreme one and creator of the world according to the Old-Testament Bible. According to the New-Testament Bible, Labbi Yeshua sacrificed himself in order to save all mortals from sin and he resurrected from the dead after three days and ascended to Heaven after fourty days. After that, he was called 'Jesus Christ' by Christians. They believe that Jesus Christ will return to the earth as the Redeemer of mortals in the last days of the world.
- According to some sayings, it is worth noting the implication that Labbi Yeshua is implied to have never been born (and potentially never even conceived) in the story world due to false Gabriel's interference.
Mark Heathcliff
Mark was an average young man. His interactions with Cesar showed he was concerned for his friends and family. He appeared to be paranoid about going over to Cesar's house, notably due to the 'THINK principle' being broadcasted to the entirety of Mandela County and its surrounding counties. The 'THINK principle' explicitly states that locking your doors and staying home was the safest approach to avoid an alternate encounter. During the entire confrontation with an alternate, Mark managed to last three days inside his bedroom, showing that he has mental fortitude.
Mark only snapped when the alternate impersonating Cesar presumably revealed the truth: Christianity's saying about Christ was a lie and humanity had been fooled from the very start. This leads him to having a mental breakdown, desperately shooting the alternate before succumbing to MAD and ending his own life.
Joseph
Joseph is seen sleeping, while someone stares at him through the window. They say, "I will fool the shepherds. I will know their greatest fear. I will know your greatest fear." Following this, they repeatedly tell Joseph to wake up. The image disappears, and the sounds of panting (possibly by Joseph himself). With closed captions on, the following is displayed:
"How frozen I became and powerless then, Ask it not, reader, for I write it not, Because all language would be insufficient. I did not die, and I alive remained not. Think for thyself now, hast though ought of wit, What I became, being of both deprived."

entries.name: Gabriel The Archangel
entries.content:
According to the mythos of Judaism and Christianity, Gabriel, like all other angels, was created by God Yehweh himself in the beginning. He was soon appointed to be an archangel.
At the beginning of Vol.4, after Adam and Eve were created, it was seen that a angel-like creature who looked like Gabriel appeared in front of Adam one night. It was heavily implied that Adam was replaced with a false one after that. It is unknown whether this so-called 'Gabriel' is true or not.
In Exhibition, a false angel pretended to be Gabriel. The video implied that this false angel tried to deceive Noah to make him refuse to build an ark which God Yehweh commanded to build. In the video, the false angel said that Noah would be punished for resisting his message, and 'another creature' would be brought on the boat. It was heavily implied this creature was the first alternate. It is unknown where true Gabriel was when this false angel impersonated him.
True Gabriel only appeared for a short time at the beginning of Overthrone. He announced to some shepherds that Yeshua, who was the son of God Yehweh, would be born later. It is heavily implied that true Gabriel was soon replaced with a false one who sabotaged the Annunciation.
It is unknown what happened to the true Gabriel after the event occurred in Overthrone. Some people said that he might have been killed by false Gabriel or might have been trapped somewhere that he could not escape.
